name: GlobalStorageComponentClientFacet_ReceiveStorageSearchItems
summary: A 38-byte body the server repeats 23 times during world entry: the shared two-u64 head, then a 16-byte raw run, then a 6-byte tail. All 23 committed records are byte-identical, so this is a broadcast of an EMPTY result repeated on a cadence, not 23 different answers. The tail is all zero, which is exactly what the reader's shape predicts for an empty item list: a prefix-varint count of 0, one u32, one flag byte.
purpose: Push the global-storage search results to the client. In the captured session it pushes nothing 23 times over. The repetition is measured and the emptiness is measured; whether the client treats an empty push as a no-op or as a state reset is not.

created_when: the server repeats it on a cadence during world entry: seqs 0x0c-0x0e and 0x11-0x24, two contiguous runs
lifecycle.if_absent: the client's storage search results never arrive. NOTE: the lab measured 23 facet-target dispatch failures for this exact wire in run exitval-194552, the same count as the 23 captured records - see the evidence below

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 followed by the wide prefix varint 88 6e, i.e. type index 7048 = 0x1b88. fields[] below use BODY offsets, so the first body byte is at 0x00 and the 42-byte record starts 4 bytes earlier.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: Measured e2 64 0b 7c e5 40 80 36 = 0xe2640b7ce5408036, identical in all 23 records. First u64 of the shared message head: the sending facet's own local id, here the global-storage client facet. This is the SAME value the atlas already pinned from the C2S side on 0x183 SetReplicateStorage, which is a cross-direction confirmation: the two directions agree that 0xe2640b7ce5408036 is the global-storage facet.
fields.provenance: msg.set-replicate-storage.json pins the same id from a client-sent record; measured corpus-wide on 2026-11-09 across 36 R records of 10 types

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Measured bf 85 31 4b bc 4a 95 1a = 0xbf85314bbc4a951a, identical in all 23 records. Second u64 of the shared head: the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id, written big-endian; read little-endian those bytes are 1a954abc4b3185bf.
fields.provenance: already earned in msg.time-sync-to-client.json (writer FUN_1414dbca0); re-measured here

fields.name: search_id
fields.note: Measured all zero in all 23 records. The reader's first act after the head is one raw 16-byte transfer into object +0x60, so the width is fourteen bytes of nothing-ambiguity and two of structure: it is exactly 16. That it is a search id is inferred from the message's name and the client's other storage replies; the value being zero everywhere means the capture carries an empty search, so no non-zero sample exists to confirm the reading. Carried as a fixed run rather than an id type because the meaning is not measured.
fields.provenance: decompile: writer FUN_142cd1f00, vtable raw-transfer slot +0x40 with length 0x10 into object +0x60; apply FUN_142cd1e00 copies the same two u64 at +0x60/+0x68

fields.name: empty_search_tail
fields.note: Measured all zero in all 23 records. The reader defines this tail exactly, and an all-zero six bytes is what its shape produces when the list is empty: FUN_140877b10 writes a prefix-varint count (here 0, the first byte), the element loop runs zero times, then one u32 BE is read (four bytes), then one flag byte is read (one byte) - 1 + 4 + 1 = 6. That the arithmetic lands on 6 with count 0 is what accounts for the whole 38-byte body. Carried as one fixed run rather than as three fields because every byte is zero and the split is therefore not separable by data; the structure is recorded in this note and in the evidence instead. A non-empty list adds 0x18-byte elements between the count and the u32, and that element layout is NOT modelled: the gate would need a card for it, and no sample has ever carried one.
fields.provenance: decompile: writer FUN_142cd1f00 after the id run - FUN_140877b10(count), loop over a std::vector at +0x38..+0x40 with stride 0x18, then FUN_140876e70(+0x34), then one raw byte from +0x30. 1+0+4+1 = 6

evidence.ref: object vtable 0x1481385c0, resolved by the name-accessor walk (its +0x08 slot is the name accessor: see the sentence that names the string). Message-object slots, using the convention meanings.md established on 2026-10-29 for 0xf37 and 0xda2, where the MARSHAL thunk 0x1414c0730 is `mov rax,[rdx]; jmp [rax+0x60]`: +0x58 = FUN_142cd1e00 is the APPLY handler, which resolves a manager singleton through FUN_1416bd7c0 and copies the value in without ever touching the stream; +0x60 = FUN_142cd1f00 is the WRITER, which serializes the body onto the stream; +0x68 = FUN_142cd20b0 is the READER, which deserializes the body off the stream

writer FUN_142cd1f00 in wire order: FUN_1414dbca0() for the shared head; the stream raw slot +0x40 with length 0x10 into object +0x60; then the list - FUN_140877b10 writes the prefix-varint count, the loop walks a vector at +0x38..+0x40 with stride 0x18 reading per element a u32 BE (FUN_140876e70) plus a presence byte and, when present, a nested object through its own vtable; then a u32 BE at +0x34; then one raw byte from +0x30. Head 16 + id 16 + count 1 + u32 4 + flag 1 = 38, which is the body width exactly

the apply FUN_142cd1e00 copies the same set in the same order into the send call: flag at +0x30, u32 at +0x34, the vector through the copy helper FUN_142cf1450 over +0x38, and the two id u64 at +0x60/+0x68. FUN_142cf1450 confirms the element stride is 0x18 (divisor in its element count), independently of the reader's loop

23 records, seqs 0x0c 0x0d 0x0e 0x11 0x12 0x13 0x14 0x15 0x16 0x17 0x18 0x19 0x1a 0x1b 0x1c 0x1d 0x1e 0x1f 0x20 0x21 0x22 0x23 0x24, each 42 bytes. A byte comparison over the set shows ONE distinct record: they are all identical, so this is one broadcast repeated 23 times, not 23 answers

operational correlation worth acting on: research/atlas/client-functions.json records that in run exitval-194552 the client logged 23 'facet target ID couldn't be found' errors for GlobalStorageComponentClientFacet_ReceiveStorageSearchItems (wire 7048), and the capture carries exactly 23 records of this wire. Same count, and this wire is the storage facet whose 16-byte id is all zero here - a zero target id cannot dispatch anywhere. NOT established as the cause: the lab's 23 errors could be the same repetition failing 23 times for an unrelated reason
